definitions.gloss: burrow; den; nest hole; an animal's underground dwelling
definitions.explanation: A hole or tunnel dug by an animal for shelter, nesting, or hibernation. Used for the homes of rabbits, foxes, badgers, moles, crabs, and other burrowing creatures.

examples.japanese: うさぎ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{巣穴|すあな}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: The rabbit went into its burrow.

examples.japanese: ⟦{狐|きつね}→狐：04337_kitsune⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{巣穴|すあな}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{子育|こそだ}て→子育て：12226_kosodate⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Foxes raise their young in their den.

examples.japanese: ⟦{砂浜|すなはま}→砂浜：12333_sunahama⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧カニ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{巣穴|すあな}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There were many crab burrows on the sandy beach.

notes:
Combines ⟦{巣|す}→巣：02140_su⟧ (nest) and ⟦{穴|あな}→穴：01691_ana⟧ (hole). A straightforward compound describing an animal's hole-type dwelling.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {巣穴|すあな}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{潜|もぐ}る→潜る：03931_moguru⟧: to burrow into a den
- {巣穴|すあな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{掘|ほ}る→掘る：00442_horu⟧: to dig a burrow
- {巣穴|すあな}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: to come out of a burrow
- {巣穴|すあな}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{逃|に}げ{込|こ}む→逃げ込む：26822_nigekomu⟧: to flee into a burrow

USAGE:
Used in nature documentaries, children's stories, and everyday descriptions of animal behavior. Can refer to any animal's underground or hole-type dwelling — rabbit warrens, fox dens, crab holes, etc. Occasionally used figuratively for a person's hiding place or private retreat.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{巣|す}→巣：02140_su⟧: nest — broader term covering all types of animal homes (bird nests, beehives, etc.), not just underground holes
- ⟦{穴|あな}→穴：01691_ana⟧: hole — a general hole in the ground, not necessarily an animal's dwelling
- ⟦{洞穴|ほらあな}→洞穴：16206_horaana⟧: cave — a natural cavity in rock, larger than a {巣穴|すあな}
